definition: An economic system where companies extract and commodify personal data from users' online activities to generate profits through targeted advertising and behavioral prediction.
metaDescription: Learn about surveillance capitalism - how tech companies monetize your personal data through tracking, profiling, and targeted advertising.
simpleExplanation: Surveillance capitalism is when companies like Google and Facebook make money by collecting vast amounts of data about your online behavior, then selling that information to advertisers who want to influence your purchasing decisions.
whyItMatters: This system turns your personal information into a commodity without your explicit consent, potentially manipulating your behavior while concentrating enormous power in the hands of a few tech giants who know more about you than you know about yourself.
technicalDetail: The system relies on extensive data collection through cookies, tracking pixels, device fingerprinting, and cross-platform identification. Machine learning algorithms process this data to create detailed behavioral profiles, predict future actions, and optimize ad targeting for maximum engagement and conversion rates.

examples.explanation: Facebook tracks your activity across millions of websites through embedded 'Like' buttons and pixels, building a profile of your interests even when you're not on Facebook, then sells access to advertisers.
Google analyzes your search queries, email content, location data, and browsing history to create detailed profiles that advertisers use to target you with personalized ads across the web.
Voice assistants like Alexa record conversations and smart TVs track viewing habits, with this data being used to refine advertising profiles and potentially sold to third parties.

niche: Economic model underlying much of the modern internet economy
